<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
In order to warm up indicators, Python algorithms needs to make a historical data request that returns a pandas DataFrame that will be used to update indicators (see also #5634). 
This approach is slow and inefficient. Python algorithms with universes that are frequently changing spend a large amount of time on warm ups. This is especially true when higher resolution data is used and/or many securities are added/removed. 

`IndicatorBatchUpdate `aims to solve this problem by avoiding the conversion from `Enumerable<Slice>` to `pandas.DataFrame` and providing Python developers an alternative to `history.PushThrough(data => indicator.Update(data))`. 

`IndicatorBatchUpdate `supports various use cases. For instance, it also works for a custom quote bar indicator if the associated security type is equity and has not yet been added to the SubscriptionManager. 

#### Limitations and other notes: 
User-defined selectors are not reflected in `IndicatorBatchUpdate`, but `ConsolidatorBatchUpdate `can be used as an alternative here. The latter offers a bit more flexibility. 

`Resolution.Tick` is not supported due to `period.GetType() = int`, see also [line 334 in QCAlgorithm.History.cs](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/9579c4263bc8681dc7d8499f8f58252aa41c917c/Algorithm/QCAlgorithm.History.cs#L334). 

#### Performance analysis: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68070194/135891365-b7b431e5-0c2d-4c6b-b47c-631c1a4dbc5f.png)


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68070194/135891347-86d26f10-d766-455c-b8bc-9200108406b0.png)


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68070194/135891324-9225266c-1b0a-4016-8b5c-6459340c35cc.png)




#### Conclusion: 
`IndicatorBatchUpdate `brings a time saving of 80% compared to the currently recommended version with DataFrames. `ConsolidatorBatchUpdate`, on the other hand, is still slightly faster, but significantly slower than `IndicatorBatchUpdate`. Please refer to #5955 for more information. A solution of #5955 should bring the performance of `ConsolidatorBatchUpdate `close to those of `IndicatorBatchUpdate`.

pr_comments: Beauty =) Thank you for the PR @ArthurAsenheimer, we'll review with some planned fixes to the Update() method as well.

Hey @ArthurAsenheimer!
Thanks for the PR, after some discussion we decided to put this PR on pause for now. We believe that ideally the API should be kept as simple as possible and solving any speed issue in the backend without the user needing to know about it/handle it. We could achieve this by caching or basically improving the operation itself.
As Alex was pointing out using a batch approach is fragile since there are many dimensions where it might not be compatible, data types, periods, symbols. 
We've recently fixed related issue https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/5943 (at https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/pull/5978) and pushed a few performance improvements for python too at https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/pull/5968 all driven by this issue at hand.
I'll close this PR for now, but keep the referenced issue https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues/5634 for the potential performance improvements for warming up indicators

issue_context.title: Implement History.PushThrough for Python Indicators
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
Be able to update a series of indicators with a single command.

#### Actual Behavior
Python algorithm needs to make a historical data request that returns a pandas DataFrame that will be used to update indicators. If the algorithm uses `EnableAutomaticIndicatorWarmUp` instead, it will make the same historical data request if there is more than one indicator per Symbol. Additionally, it will not warm up chained indicators (e.g.: `IndicatorExtensions.Of`), because they are not supported (there is no chain `WarmupPeriod`).
In C#, this is easily handled with 
```csharp
History(symbol, period, resolution).PushThrough(bar => indicator.Update(bar.EndTime, bar.Price));
```

#### Potential Solution
Implement a method that updates a list of indicators:
E.g.:
```python
self.IndicatorBatchUpdate(symbol, period, resolution, indicators)
```

#### Checklist
- [x] I have completely filled out this template
- [x] I have confirmed that this issue exists on the current `master` branch
- [x] I have confirmed that this is not a duplicate issue by searching [issues](https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/issues)

review_comments:
In retrospect, it seems unnecessary to split it into two separate and differently named methods (`IndicatorBatchUpdate `and `ConsolidatorBatchUpdate`). I think we should use method overloading. `ConsolidatorBatchUpdate `seems to me to be the better choice here because the term is more general and includes both. 
What do you think?

In some cases, the minimum number of samples that an indicator needs to be fully warmed up is not trivial, so the user might provide a period that is not big enough. Consequently, the `period` should be defined by the maximum value of `IIndicatorWarmUpPeriodProvider.WarmUpPeriod` (see `GetIndicatorWarmUpHistory` for reference), and this parameter can be removed.

I've been thinking about that, too. But what about custom python indicators which don't have a `WarmUpPeriod` as far as I know? Maybe a better solution would be setting `int period = 0` as default and if the provided period is zero, we use the approach you described. What do you think?
